data.name: Nivetha
data.gender_notes: Nivetha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Nivetha is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Nivethana', which means 'New Birth' or 'Fresh Beginning'. It is believed that this name was given to babies born during the Navratri festival, symbolizing the renewal of life and the blessings of the nine Goddesses. The name Nivetha carries the meaning “New Birth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nivetha usually hope their child will grow to embody new birth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Nivetha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “New Birth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nivetha total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nivetha holds a deep cultural significance in Hinduism, especially in South India, where it is popularly used. The name is associated with the Navratri festival, a significant and widely celebrated occasion in Hinduism. The festival celebrates the nine forms of Goddess Durga, who are believed to bestow their blessings and protection on their devotees, infusing them with new energy, strength, courage, and knowledge.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Nivetha carries the profound meaning of new birth and fresh beginnings. The prefix 'Niveth' denotes the idea of rejuvenation, renewal, and the beginning of a new phase in life. It is a name that signifies the cyclical nature of life, the inner transformation that occurs when we shed our old self and embrace a new day, a new identity, and a new purpose.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nivetha, meaning 'pure and sacred offering,' signifies an individual who strives to make every action and thought a dedication to the divine. This name embodies the purity and devotion inherent in Hindu spirituality.
